message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 bar) the melting/freezing point of water is **about –2 °C**.

**Why?**  
The phase diagram of water shows that the melting point decreases with decreasing pressure. At the triple‑point pressure (≈6.1 kPa) ice, liquid water, and vapor coexist at –0.01 °C. As you increase the pressure from the triple point toward 100 kPa, the melting point rises linearly to 0 °C at 100 kPa. Interpolating between the triple point and 100 kPa gives roughly –2 °C at 10 kPa.

So if you cool liquid water down to about –2 °C while keeping the pressure at 10 kPa, it will start to freeze.
